reason: Gives the maximum conducted transient pulse amplitudes (+75 V/-100 V for 12 V systems, +150 V/-450 V for 24 V systems) that the ACPE electronic sub-assemblies (powertrain control unit, sensors) must not exceed on supply lines.
Marking requirement on the ACPE ESA (control unit/sensors) samples: they must be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
Each ESA of the ACPE system (sensors, camera, control unit) approved as a component must carry the R10 approval mark.
Approval mark must include a circle with letter E and the number of the approving country.
Approval mark must include the regulation number, the letter R, a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle.
ACPE electronics must be designed, built and fitted so the vehicle meets R10 EMC requirements in normal use.
ACPE ESAs must be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
Immunity field strength and BCI current levels the vehicle with the installed ACPE must withstand.
ACPE limits propulsion torque, an immunity-related function, so it must show no performance degradation during immunity tests.
ESA broadband radiated emission limit values by frequency band.
Measured ESA broadband emissions must be below the type-approval limits.
ESA narrowband radiated emission limit values by frequency band.
Measured ESA narrowband emissions must be below the type-approval limits.
The ACPE ESAs (control unit, sensors, camera) on the 12 V supply must meet the transient conducted emission levels of Table 1 per ISO 7637-2 / Annex 10.
Sets the radiated immunity test levels (Tables 2a/2b, 20–6,000 MHz) the ACPE ESAs must withstand.
Pass criterion: no degradation of immunity related functions. ACPE affects propulsion torque, so this applies.
Sets the conducted transient immunity levels and the functional status classes (starting profile, pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b; Tables 3a/3b) for the ACPE ESAs on the 12 V supply.
Sets the radiated immunity field strengths (30 V/m and 10 V/m bands) and the 60 mA BCI current. The ACPE sensors, camera and powertrain control unit must withstand these levels.
Pass criterion: no degradation of immunity-related functions during the radiated immunity test. ACPE limits propulsion torque and warns the driver, so it counts as an immunity-related function.
Broadband radiated emission limits (62–52 / 52–63 / 63 dBµV/m, 30–1000 MHz) apply to the ACPE control unit, camera and ultrasonic sensors as ESAs.
Requires the measured broadband emission values of the ACPE ESA to stay below the type approval limits.
The ACPE control unit is microprocessor-based, so its narrowband radiated emissions must stay within the limits across 30–1,000 MHz.
The vehicle, including the ACPE electronics and wiring, must withstand the radiated immunity field levels of para 6.4.2.1 while being monitored for correct function.
Defines the 50 km/h-mode immunity failure criteria (speed variation, unexpected cluster warnings) that the ACPE torque intervention, tell-tale and buzzer must not trigger under radiated disturbance.
REESS charging-mode failure criteria (vehicle sets in motion, loss of parking position) apply to the hybrid/BEV variants, where ACPE runs in the powertrain control unit that commands propulsion.
Specifies the radiated immunity exposure (20–6000 MHz, vertical polarization, AM/PM2/PM3 modulation) that the ACPE sensors, camera and control unit must withstand without failure.
The broadband radiated emission limits apply to the ACPE ESAs (sensors, camera, control unit) across 30–1,000 MHz.
The narrowband radiated emission limits apply to the microprocessor-based ACPE control unit and sensors across 30–1,000 MHz.
The ACPE ESAs must show radiated immunity compliance using ISO 11452 test methods that together cover the full specified frequency range.
The ACPE ESA must be switched on and running in normal operation during radiated immunity testing, so the supplier must provide a way to stimulate it.
Sets the immunity frequency range (20–6,000 MHz) and the AM/PM modulation the ACPE control unit and sensors must withstand.
The ACPE ESA's 12 V supply connections must withstand ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, plus the ISO 16750-2 starting profile on petrol and hybrid variants that have a starter.
The ACPE control unit and sensors are ESAs on the 12 V supply, so their transient conducted emissions on supply and connected lines must be measured to ISO 7637-2.
Core function: limit unintended acceleration on misapplication with an obstacle ahead (forward) or behind (rearwards).
Defines the pedal-misapplication trigger thresholds: velocity at least 400 %/s over at least 70 % of travel, reaching at least 90 % position.
ACPE must control acceleration when accelerating from standstill.
Driver must be told if ACPE is not ready 6 s after powertrain initiation, until it initialises.
Must prevent or mitigate collision with an obstacle 1.0–1.5 m ahead or behind, under the stated conditions.
Collision speed limits: no more than +8 km/h over trigger speed and no more than 70 % of the speed without ACPE.
Acceleration must stay limited throughout an intervention; sets the conditions for ending it.
EMC immunity per UN R10 06 series.
Electronic control system safety requirements per Annex 3 apply to the ACPE.
Driver must be informed of an intervention.
Driver must be able to interrupt the intervention by an intentional action.
No rapid increase of acceleration when the driver interrupts by keeping the pedal applied.
Manual deactivation is fitted: ACPE must reinstate at each new engine start, with a warning at the time of deactivation.
Failure warning required for any ACPE failure that prevents compliance.
Self-check frequency and no delay in the warning, with the 10 km/h suppression allowance.
Failure warning also required for non-electrical failures such as sensor blindness or misalignment.
Optical warnings must be visible in daylight and verifiable from the driver's seat.
Optical warning signals must activate at power-on (bulb check).
Intervention warning must be optical plus haptic or acoustic.
Failure warning must be a constant yellow optical signal.
For periodic technical inspection, the failure warning must stay lit after power-on if a failure persists from the previous cycle.
Failure warning operation must be protected against simple unauthorised modification.

Defines the misapplication test scenarios the ACPE must pass: with and without expected intervention, in both forward and rearward directions, starting 1.0 m and 1.5 m from the target with 0–0.2 m lateral offset. These set the supplier's verification cases for the obstacle-detection and torque-suppression function.

Requires that the ACPE electronic control system meet all performance requirements under both non-fault and fault conditions and be designed so that it does not induce safety-critical risks; this is a design obligation for the system's safety concept.
Each ACPE unit (sensors, camera, control unit software) must carry clear, unambiguous hardware/software identification marking, with a single marking per combined unit.
The identification must define the hardware and software version and be changed whenever a software change alters the regulated ACPE function.
On an ACPE failure the driver must be warned, and the warning must persist as long as the fault exists unless the system is deactivated; this matches the spec's fault reporting.
